sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction
sections.body:
## Purpose
The Patient Portal extends the Hospital EMR patient management system to provide patients with secure, web‑based access to their health information.

## Scope
The portal will enable patients to view personal health records, schedule appointments, and communicate with care teams while ensuring compliance with HIPAA regulations.

## Definitions
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record system used by the hospital.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, governing protection of PHI.

*Initial draft note:* Initial draft of requirements.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
The Patient Portal is a thin client web application that interfaces with the existing Hospital EMR backend via secure APIs. It resides within the hospital’s DMZ and leverages the hospital’s authentication services (e.g., LDAP/Active Directory). The architecture consists of:
- **Presentation Layer**: Browser‑based UI.
- **Application Layer**: Web server handling business logic.
- **Data Access Layer**: Secure connectors to the EMR database.
All components must operate under the hospital’s security policies and network segmentation.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: Functional behavior to be defined by stakeholders.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements
table: System shall respond to user actions within 250 ms for the 95th percentile of requests.
Load testing with realistic traffic profiles
All patient data must be encrypted at rest using AES‑256 as required by HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(i).
All access and modification events must be recorded in tamper‑evident audit logs per HIPAA §164.312(b).

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### User Interface
- Web‑based responsive UI accessible via modern browsers.

### Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)
- Secure RESTful APIs to retrieve and update patient data from the EMR system. All API calls must use TLS 1.2+.

### Hardware Interfaces
- No dedicated hardware required; the portal runs on standard hospital web servers within the existing infrastructure.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
#### Constraints
- Must operate within the hospital’s network security zones.
- Must not store PHI on client devices.
- Must adhere to the hospital’s change‑management process.

#### Compliance Verification
- **HIPAA**: Encryption at rest (AES‑256) and audit logging will be validated through a third‑party compliance audit referencing HIPAA §164.312.
- **Performance**: Latency benchmark (P95 < 250 ms) will be verified via load‑testing scripts.
- **Security Testing**: Penetration testing and vulnerability scanning will be performed before release.

All verification results will be documented and reviewed during the formal acceptance process.
